subject: Accounting
title: Tax Audits
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tax Audits usable.

hook.text: A letter from the IRS: 'We're auditing your tax return.' Six words that ruin anyone's week.

buildup.text: Tax audits verify that taxpayers—individuals or businesses—reported income and deductions correctly.

discovery.text: They range from simple mail inquiries to full field audits where agents visit your office.

twist.text: Only about 0.4% of individual returns get audited—but the rate jumps for higher incomes.

climax.text: Good record-keeping is the best defense. Most audits end without penalties if records are solid.

punchline.text: Keep your receipts. The taxman might ask for them.

quiz.question: What percentage of individual U.S. tax returns are audited?

details.summary: Tax audits are examinations by tax authorities — like the IRS — to verify that taxpayers have correctly reported their income, deductions, and tax liability, ensuring compliance with tax law and deterring evasion.
details.whyItMatters: The possibility of a tax audit is the primary enforcement mechanism for voluntary compliance. Understanding what triggers audits and how they work reduces anxiety and helps taxpayers maintain proper records.
takeaways: Tax audits verify that reported income, deductions, and credits comply with tax law
The IRS audits less than 1% of returns annually, with higher rates for high-income filers and certain red flags
Common triggers include large deductions, unreported income, round numbers, and statistical anomalies

faq.question: What triggers a tax audit?
faq.answer: Common triggers include unusually large deductions relative to income, discrepancies between reported income and third-party reports (W-2s, 1099s), high income, cash-heavy businesses, and statistical outliers flagged by IRS algorithms. Random selection also accounts for a small percentage.

faq.question: What should you do if you're audited?
faq.answer: Respond promptly and provide only the documents specifically requested. Keep organized records throughout the year so you can support every deduction and income item. Consider hiring a tax professional to represent you. Never ignore an audit notice — failure to respond leads to much worse outcomes.
